timeline: You assume automated nuclear defense systems are infallible, until a single officer decides to ignore a five-missile warning on September 26, 1983.
On 26 September 1983, five missiles flashed on screen.
Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov stared at the glowing console.
Protocol demanded an immediate retaliatory nuclear strike.
But an all-out American attack would involve hundreds of missiles.
Petrov decided to wait instead of calling his superiors.
Minutes passed. No actual explosions shook the Soviet Union.
Investigators later found sunlight on clouds tricked the satellites.
He was reprimanded for improper filing in the military diary and took early retirement.
He disobeyed protocol and saved the world from catastrophe.
